title: IMDC (International Metastatic RCC Database Consortium) risque modèle pour Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma
formula:
Addition of the selected points:

| Variable | Points |
| --- | --- |
| <1 year from time of diagnosis to systemic therapy | 1 |
| [Karnofsky performance status](nabda:calc.karnofsky-performance-status-scale\) <80% | 1 |
| Hemoglobin < lower limit of normal (usually ~120 g/L or 12 g/dL) | 1 |
| [Corrected calcium](nabda:calc.calcium-correction-hypoalbuminemia\) > upper limit of normal (usually ~8.5-10.2 mg/dL) | 1 |
| Neutrophils > upper limit of normal (usually ~2.0-7.0×10⁹/L) | 1 |
| Platelets > upper limit of normal (usually ~150,000-400,000 cells/µL) | 1 |

how_to_use.why: Aide les cliniciens dans les discussions sur le pronostic et dans le choix du traitement systémique approprié chez les patients atteints d’un carcinome rénal métastatique.
how_to_use.when: Patients atteints d’un carcinome à cellules rénales métastatique.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Validé dans les contextes suivants :
- Peut aider au choix d’un traitement systémique.
- Facile à utiliser, repose sur des variables cliniques et biologiques facilement disponibles, et se compare favorablement à d’autres modèles similaires de prédiction du pronostic.

next_steps.critical_actions: Ne peut être appliqué qu'aux patients atteints d'un carcinome à cellules rénales métastatique recevant un traitement systémique.
next_steps.management:
According to[NCCN guidelines (v3.2019)](https://www.nccn.org/professionals/physician_gls/default.aspx), choice of first-line systemic therapy for metastatic renal cell carcinoma based on risk group is:

- **Intermediate or poor risk** : ipilimumab plus nivolumab (Phase III trial evidence) or cabozantinib (Phase II trial evidence).
- **Favorable risk** : PAZOPanib or SUNItinib.

Refer toAUA guidelinesfor further details on management of renal cancer.

evidence:
The International Metastatic RCC Database Consortium (IMDC) risk model was initially derived from a 2009 study of 645 patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma treated with first-line targeted therapy in 3 US and 4 Canadian centers ([Heng 2009](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/19826129)). The model showed a concordance index (C-index) of 0.73 and patients classified into the different risk groups had significantly different overall survival.

The model was subsequently externally validated ([Heng 2013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4144042/)) in 849 consecutive patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma from 13 international cancer centres and was shown to compare favorably to 4 other risk models used in this setting: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (MSKCC) model, Cleveland Clinic Foundation (CCF) model, French model, and International Kidney Cancer Working Group (IKCWG) model.

The model has also been validated in patients with non-clear cell renal cell carcinoma ([Kroeger 2013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/23696129)), subsequent lines of therapy ([Ko 2015](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25681967),[Wells 2017](https://www.europeanurology.com/article/S0302-2838(16)30258-5/fulltext)), and patients treated by immune checkpoint inhibitors ([Yip 2017](https://ascopubs.org/doi/abs/10.1200/JCO.2017.35.6_suppl.492)).

Specific IMDC risk groups have also been shown to have better outcomes with certain systemic therapies. In particular, the IMDC intermediate and poor risk groups should be preferentially treated with first line nivolumab + ipilimumab or cabozantinib therapy ([Motzer 2018](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/29562145),[Choueiri 2017](https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/JCO.2016.70.7398),[NCCN guidelines v3.2019](https://www.nccn.org/professionals/physician_gls/default.aspx)). Thus, IMDC risk groups have also become a tool for the selection of systemic therapy for first line clear cell metastatic renal cell carcinoma patients.
more_info:
Interprétation :

| Score de risque IMDC | Groupe de risque | Survie médiane |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Favorable | 43,2 mois |
| 1-2 | Intermédiaire | 22,5 mois |
| ≥3 | Défavorable | 7,8 mois |

D'après [Heng 2013](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4144042/).
